---
title: "Genetic parameters for each group"
description: >
  Several populations (herds, breeds, lines) in one data set, with
  heritabilities and other parameters estimated separately for each group -
  and for all groups together for comparison.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

[中文版](parameters-by-group-zh.html)

When the data hold several populations, the genetic parameters often differ
between them. The usual table is "h² (SE) of every trait in every group".
With mintyrasr this is one nested table and one call; no cross-validation is
needed (`cv = NULL`, the default).

## Data

One row per individual, with the group column (here `test_herd`), the fixed
effects and the traits:

```{r}
library(asreml)
library(mintyr)
library(mintyrasr)

pheno <- import_xlsx("pheno.xlsx")      # id, test_herd, hhys, sex, adg, bf, fcr
```

## Single-trait parameters per group

`w2l_nest(by = "test_herd")` makes one data set per trait and group:

```{r}
nest <- w2l_nest(pheno, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr"), by = "test_herd", out_type = "df")
nest                                     # name | test_herd | data

res <- asr_gblup(nest, ginv = ginv, fixed = ~ hhys + sex, inbreeding = inbreeding,
                 path = "h2_by_herd.xlsx")
res$param[, .(name, test_herd, h2, h2_se, status, boundary)]
```

A report table, traits in rows and groups in columns:

```{r}
library(data.table)
p <- res$param[, .(name, test_herd, txt = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", h2, h2_se))]
dcast(p, name ~ test_herd, value.var = "txt")
```

Any model of [Beyond the animal model](other-models.html) works the same way,
e.g. `random = ~ litter` adds `prop_litter` per group. Pedigree or single-step
analyses only need another matrix (see
[A, G and H](relationship-matrices.html)).

## All groups together

For comparison, the same traits with all groups in one model; the group
effect is in the fixed effects (here through `hhys`, which is nested in herd):

```{r}
all <- w2l_nest(pheno, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr"), out_type = "df")
res_all <- asr_gblup(all, ginv = ginv, fixed = ~ hhys + sex, inbreeding = inbreeding)
res_all$param[, .(name, h2, h2_se)]
```

To test whether the genetic variance differs between groups, or how well the
groups are genetically connected, see the G×E part of
[Beyond the animal model](other-models.html) and
[The same trait in different populations](same-trait-across-groups.html).

## Two-trait parameters per group

`c2p_nest(by = "test_herd")` gives every trait pair in every group; see
[Correlations between traits in each population](correlations-between-traits.html).

## Points to watch

- **Group size.** Small groups give large SEs and estimates at the boundary
  (h² = 0). Check `status`, `boundary` and `res$log`; a component fixed at
  the boundary is listed there.
- **Fixed effects per group.** Contemporary groups usually differ between
  groups; with one model per group each group gets its own levels anyway.
- **Same model in all groups**, so that the estimates are comparable; if one
  group needs a different model, run it separately.
- **GEBVs per group** are in `res$gebv` (with `reliable = rel >= min_rel`).
